'Not a stand-in for: a crosswalk' does not apply.

st.obstruction is 'a physical object on or beside the roadway that is not a road user'; 'encounters' is ego at the obstruction while on the sidewalk: drv.position.near_region(ego, o) with p.obstruction_reach, over the body-to-region distance of st.region_geometry, the anchor of the obstruction to ego. 'to his or her mobility' is read through ego's conduct at it (s8).

Nearest atoms only, to show the shortfall (gap on s4): a missing section of sidewalk is no 'physical object' (st.obstruction), and the absence of a sidewalk region (st.sidewalk) is not a stretch a source records that a pedestrian meets.

'may proceed' is ego's travel off the sidewalk: its footprint overlaps (rel.occupies) a region of kind st.travel_region ('a lane ..., a bicycle lane or path, a roadway ..., a shoulder, or an intersection'), which excludes 'a sidewalk'.

'the immediately adjacent highway' is the same way as the sidewalk: the travel region ego occupies and the sidewalk both lie on one highway region (st.on_way; st.highway 'including sidewalks and shoulders'); belonging is read through st.on_way, never a distance ('Not a stand-in for: nearness to a way').
A purpose read through the conduct it explains (observable_reading purpose): since the last observation at which ego occupied the sidewalk while at that obstruction, ego has occupied no sidewalk.
'Such a pedestrian' is the pedestrian of s1 proceeding under the first sentence: the same binder and aggregate.

'as far to the side of the highway near the sidewalk' is ego's position across the way relative to the sidewalk: the ground distance from ego's body outline to the sidewalk region (st.region_geometry, 'the ground distance from a road user's body outline to it'), the sidewalk being the one ego left (s2, re-bound). 'a lane provided for bicycles, electric bicycles or electric scooters' is st.bicycle_lane_or_path, 'lane or separate path reserved for bicycles and the devices a jurisdiction groups with them'; ego's footprint overlapping it (rel.occupies). operationalizations.convention: Lateral position at the edge: the body-to-sidewalk distance (st.region_geometry) is at or below p.pedestrian_edge_margin, a step's width plus the shy distance a walker keeps from a curb; where an obstruction lies across ego's side toward the sidewalk (prim.region_lateral_offset of the obstruction of the same sign as the sidewalk's and of smaller magnitude), the nearest thing ego can keep to is that obstruction, and its body-to-obstruction distance is held to the same margin. The obstruction's own lateral reach moves the bound.

An area is impassable on foot where a physical object blocks it: an obstruction lies laterally between ego and the sidewalk (prim.region_lateral_offset of the obstruction of the same sign as the sidewalk's and of smaller magnitude) and within p.obstruction_reach of ego (drv.position.near_region over st.region_geometry).

applicability: As NRS_484B_297_6_o1: ego is a pedestrian; at the judged observation ego occupies no sidewalk and occupies a travel region lying on a highway h on which a sidewalk s also lies, and since the last observation at which ego occupied s while at an obstruction (drv.position.near_region with p.obstruction_reach), ego has occupied no sidewalk. obligation: For the sidewalk s selected as in the applicability (re-bound with the same relations): the distance from ego's body to s (st.region_geometry) is at or below p.pedestrian_edge_margin, or an obstruction o lies laterally between ego and s (prim.region_lateral_offset of o of the same sign as that of s and of smaller magnitude) and the distance from ego's body to o is at or below p.pedestrian_edge_margin.

'impassable' is read only through a physical object between the bicycle lane and the sidewalk; a strip impassable for other reasons (standing vehicles, a drop-off) is not read.

segmentation.text: Where the signal is a steady red with a green turn arrow:
A person driving a motorcycle, moped
or trimobile
or riding a bicycle, an electric bicycle or an electric scooter
facing the signal
may proceed straight through or turn in the direction opposite that indicated by the green turn arrow
if:

(1) The person stops before entering the crosswalk on the nearest side of the intersection where the sign or pavement marking indicates where the stop must be made or, in the absence of any such crosswalk, sign or marking, before entering the intersection;
(2) The person waits for two complete cycles of the lights or lighted arrows of the applicable official traffic-control device and the signal does not change
because of a malfunction or because the signal failed to detect the presence of the motorcycle, moped, trimobile, bicycle, electric bicycle or electric scooter;
(3) No other device at the place prohibits the turn,
if applicable;
and
(4) The person yields the right-of-way to pedestrians lawfully within an adjacent crosswalk and to other traffic lawfully using the intersection.

elements.justification: dev.traffic_signal is 'a signal head; state ∈ {..., circular_red, green_arrow(dir), ...}' and 'several states may be displayed at once': a steady red with a green turn arrow is circular_red displayed together with green_arrow(left), green_arrow(right) or green_arrow(u_turn); 'steady' excludes flashing_red, 'turn' excludes green_arrow(straight). Read at ego's entry into the intersection, the event the words fix it to.

'motorcycle' is admitted as DEF-NRS-484A-135::motorcycle ('every motor vehicle equipped with a seat or saddle for the use of the driver and designed to travel on not more than three wheels'); 'moped' as DEF-NRS-484A-125::moped ('a motor-driven scooter, motor-driven cycle or similar vehicle that is propelled by a small engine'); each claimed whole. 'A person driving' is read through the vehicle's controlled motion (observable_reading agency).

Nearest atom only, to show the shortfall (gap on b3): no definition applies to 'trimobile', and ru.motorcycle ('motor vehicle on two or three wheels ridden astride, including three-wheeled variants') leaves out a three-wheeler seated in a cabin or side by side, which the word admits; ru.motor_vehicle would admit every car.

'bicycle' admitted as DEF-NRS-484A-025::bicycle ('a device propelled by human power upon which a person may ride'), 'electric bicycle' as DEF-NRS-484B-017::electric_bicycle ('a device upon which a person may ride ... an electric motor which produces not more than 750 watts'), 'electric scooter' as DEF-NRS-484B-018::electric_scooter ('a vehicle with handlebars and an electric motor'); each claimed whole.

'facing the signal': the signal controls the approach ego enters through. dev.governs is 'the travel regions whose traffic the device controls ... or an intersection'; the approach is a carrier ego occupies (rel.occupies) whose entrance end is the intersection (st.lane_enters: 'a road user's approach to an intersection is a carrier it occupies whose entrance end is that intersection'); its kind is st.travel_region. No halt place is read from dev.governs ('Not a stand-in for: a position').

'proceed straight through or turn in the direction opposite that indicated by the green turn arrow' is the movement ego makes through the intersection (st.intersection, 'the region where two roadways meet'; entered and left through rel.occupies): its heading change since entering it (drv.motion.heading_change_since_entry, which takes the intersection as its region formal) read at the exit, lying in the straight band (neither turn band) or in the turn band opposite a displayed green arrow (dev.traffic_signal green_arrow(dir)): the right band under a left arrow, the left band under a right arrow.

'stops' where a stop is required is DEF-NRS-484A-255, 'complete cessation from movement', carried by drv.motion.at_rest (DEF-NRS-484A-260 states its own scope, 'when prohibited', and does not apply). The places, in the words' order: 'where the sign or pavement marking indicates where the stop must be made' is the stop line (st.stop_line, 'the transverse line marking where vehicles halt for a device') recorded as marking the entrance of ego's carrier (st.entrance_of, 'the carrier whose entrance into an intersection a stop line or a crosswalk marks'); 'the crosswalk on the nearest side of the intersection' is the crosswalk (st.crosswalk) recorded as marking that entrance; 'before entering the intersection' is the carrier's entrance end (st.lane_enters). 'before entering' is ego short of the place along the carrier's direction (sign of prim.region_offset_along), its footprint not overlapping a crosswalk or the intersection (rel.occupies), within the stop-point tolerance (body-to-mark distance, st.region_geometry). The association is never inferred from distance.

applicability: ego is a motorcycle, moped, bicycle, electric bicycle or electric scooter (the admitted aggregates; trimobile: gap on b3). The judged observation is one at which ego leaves an intersection I (ego occupies I at the observation before and not at the judged one), whose last entry (the rise of ego's occupancy of I with no later rise, read through a since operator) took place while ego occupied a carrier c entering I (st.lane_enters(c, I)) governed by a traffic signal d (dev.governs(d, c) or dev.governs(d, I)) displaying circular_red together with green_arrow(left), green_arrow(right) or green_arrow(u_turn) at that entry observation; and ego's heading change since that entry (drv.motion.heading_change_since_entry(ego, I) with p.heading_since_step_carla_scene_graph), read at the exit, is not in the band of a displayed green turn arrow: it is in the straight band (above the negative of p.right_turn_min_angle and below p.left_turn_min_angle), or in the right band (at or below the negative of p.right_turn_min_angle and at or above the negative of p.right_turn_max_angle) where green_arrow(left) was displayed, or in the left band (at or above p.left_turn_min_angle and at or below p.left_turn_max_angle) where green_arrow(right) was displayed.
obligation: Rule 4c, by the ontology's approach convention for an act due at a place before an event. For I, c and d selected as in the applicability (re-bound with the same relations), at the judged exit: the event is ego's entry into I through c (the rise of ego's occupancy of I). The place is, in the words' order: a stop line recorded as marking c (st.entrance_of(line, c)); where every stop line's entrances are observed and none marks c, a crosswalk recorded as marking c; where neither marks c, c's entrance end at I. The act is ego at rest (drv.motion.at_rest with p.rest_speed_tolerance) short of the place along c's designated direction (sign of prim.region_offset_along with st.lane_direction of c), within p.stop_point_tolerance of it (body-to-mark distance, st.region_geometry), and, for a crosswalk or the intersection, with its footprint not overlapping that region (rel.occupies). The search runs back from the entry observation and ends only at the approach start (the last observation before the entry at which ego, on a carrier the governing mark is recorded as marking, is outside the mark's stopping zone upstream: off it, short of it and farther from it than p.stop_point_tolerance) or at ego's previous entry into I through such a carrier; nothing else ends it (not the start of the recording, not a first observation, not a distance travelled). Act found: met; an end reached without the act: violated; neither end reached and no act found: unknown. Where a mark's association with c is not observed, whether it governs is unknown, and the duty is unknown unless the verdict is the same at every candidate place.

narrowings.why: 'A person driving' (and 'riding', b4) is read through the vehicle's controlled motion: the duty binds the vehicle's conduct whoever controls it.

The words are read as listing the stop places in order: the marked stop place, else the near crosswalk, else the intersection. A sign indicating where to stop is read through the stop line it accompanies; a sign with no line is not read.

Read at ego's entry into the intersection, the event the words fix it to.

'traffic' is admitted as DEF-NRS-484A-285::traffic: 'pedestrians, ridden or herded animals, vehicles and other conveyances either singly or together using any highway for purposes of travel'. The law's own qualifier 'vehicular' limits the members the duty reads and leaves out pedestrians (and ridden or herded animals, which no class atom carries): carried beside the aggregate as the condition that ego is not ru.pedestrian ('a person on foot, in a wheelchair, or on a device the jurisdiction treats as on foot'). Its exclusion 'Not a stand-in for: a person on a bicycle or scooter' is why riders of bicycles and scooters remain vehicular traffic, as paragraph (b) confirms by excepting them.

'facing the signal': the signal controls the approach ego enters through. dev.governs is 'the travel regions whose traffic the device controls ... or an intersection'; the approach is a carrier ego occupies (rel.occupies) whose entrance end is the intersection (st.lane_enters: 'a road user's approach to an intersection is a carrier it occupies whose entrance end is that intersection'); its kind is st.travel_region, which dev.governs and st.lane_enters range over. No halt place is read ('Not a stand-in for: a position').

'enter the intersection' is the observation at which ego's footprint comes to overlap (rel.occupies) the intersection (st.intersection, 'the region where two roadways meet, bounded by the prolongation of their edges', which carries DEF-NRS-484A-105's 'area embraced within the prolongation or connection of the lateral curb lines' and its exclusion of an alley junction), the region the words single out.

'the movement indicated by the green turn arrow' is the turn whose direction the displayed arrow names (dev.traffic_signal green_arrow(dir)); the movement ego makes is its heading change since entering the intersection (drv.motion.heading_change_since_entry, which takes the intersection as its region formal), read at the exit and bounded by the reading's turn bands: the left band for a left arrow, the right band for a right arrow, the reversal band for a U-turn arrow.

residues.why: An advisory to drivers turning with the arrow about the signal opposing traffic faces: it imposes no duty and states no condition of this one, so the duty is the same whether or not its words hold.

applicability: ego is traffic (ru.aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-285::traffic) and not a pedestrian (ru.pedestrian). The judged observation is one at which ego leaves an intersection I (ego occupies I at the observation before and not at the judged one), whose last entry (the rise of ego's occupancy of I with no later rise, read through a since operator) took place while ego occupied a carrier c of kind st.travel_region entering I (st.lane_enters(c, I)) and a traffic signal d governing c or I (dev.governs) displayed circular_red together with green_arrow(left), green_arrow(right) or green_arrow(u_turn) at that entry observation. obligation: For the intersection I and signal d selected as in the applicability (re-bound with the same relations): ego's heading change since its entry into I (drv.motion.heading_change_since_entry(ego, I) with p.heading_since_step_carla_scene_graph), read at the judged exit, lies in the band of a green turn arrow d displayed at that entry: at or above p.left_turn_min_angle and at or below p.left_turn_max_angle where green_arrow(left) was displayed; at or below the negative of p.right_turn_min_angle and at or above the negative of p.right_turn_max_angle where green_arrow(right) was displayed; with magnitude at or above p.u_turn_min_angle and at or below p.u_turn_max_angle where green_arrow(u_turn) was displayed. segmentation.text: Where the signal is a steady red with a green turn arrow:
Except as otherwise provided in paragraph (b) [NRS-484B-307-9b],
vehicular traffic
facing the signal
may enter the intersection
only to make the movement indicated by the green turn arrow,
but must yield the right-of-way to pedestrians lawfully within an adjacent crosswalk and to other traffic lawfully using the intersection.
Drivers turning in the direction of the arrow are thereby advised that so long as the turn arrow is illuminated, oncoming or opposing traffic simultaneously faces a steady red signal.

elements.justification: dev.traffic_signal is 'a signal head; state ∈ {..., circular_red, green_arrow(dir), ...}' and 'several states may be displayed at once': circular_red displayed together with green_arrow(left), green_arrow(right) or green_arrow(u_turn); 'steady' excludes flashing_red and 'turn' excludes green_arrow(straight). Read at ego's entry into the intersection.

'traffic' is admitted as DEF-NRS-484A-285::traffic: 'pedestrians, ridden or herded animals, vehicles and other conveyances ... using any highway for purposes of travel'. The qualifier 'vehicular' leaves out pedestrians, carried beside the aggregate as the condition that ego is not ru.pedestrian ('a person on foot, in a wheelchair, or on a device the jurisdiction treats as on foot'); riders of bicycles and scooters stay in ('Not a stand-in for: a person on a bicycle or scooter').

'facing the signal': dev.governs ('the travel regions whose traffic the device controls ... or an intersection') of the carrier ego occupies (rel.occupies) whose entrance end is the intersection (st.lane_enters); the carrier's kind is st.travel_region. No halt place is read ('Not a stand-in for: a position').

'enter the intersection' is the observation at which ego's footprint comes to overlap (rel.occupies) the intersection (st.intersection, 'the region where two roadways meet'), the region the words single out.

'must yield the right-of-way': DEF-NRS-484A-210 makes the right-of-way the right to proceed in preference to one 'approaching under such circumstances of direction, speed and proximity as to give rise to the danger of a crash unless one grants precedence'; yielding is ego at rest (drv.motion.at_rest, as the mapping index maps 'shall yield') wherever that danger stands, read as a projected approach of the centres within the horizon (prim.closest_approach_within) to below the clearance (prim.closest_approach_distance). 'pedestrians' is DEF-NRS-484A-165::pedestrian ('a person afoot, a person in a manual or motorized wheelchair ...'); 'within an adjacent crosswalk' is the pedestrian's footprint overlapping (rel.occupies) a crosswalk (st.crosswalk, 'marked crossing, or the unmarked prolongation of sidewalks at an intersection') that marks the entrance (st.entrance_of) of a carrier (st.travel_region) entering the intersection ego occupies (st.lane_enters), every crossing of its approaches, tied by relation atoms, never by distance; 'other traffic' is DEF-NRS-484A-285::traffic other than ego, 'using the intersection' its footprint overlapping the intersection (st.intersection). 'lawfully' is not read (narrowing).

residues.why: An advisory to drivers turning with the arrow about the signal opposing traffic faces: it imposes no duty and states no condition of this one, so the duty is the same whether or not its words hold.

applicability: ego is traffic (ru.aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-285::traffic) and not a pedestrian (ru.pedestrian). At the judged observation ego occupies an intersection I, has occupied it at every observation since its last entry into it, and at that entry (the rise of ego's occupancy of I, read through a since operator) ego occupied a carrier c of kind st.travel_region entering I (st.lane_enters(c, I)) governed by a traffic signal d (dev.governs of c or I) displaying circular_red together with green_arrow(left), green_arrow(right) or green_arrow(u_turn).
obligation: For the intersection I selected as in the applicability (re-bound with the same relations): ego is at rest (drv.motion.at_rest with p.rest_speed_tolerance), or both: for every road user p other than ego that is a pedestrian (ru.aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-165::pedestrian) and occupies a crosswalk w marking the entrance of a carrier e that enters I (st.entrance_of(w, e), st.lane_enters(e, I)), it is not the case that their centres approach within p.conflict_horizon (prim.closest_approach_within) with a centre distance at that closest approach below p.pedestrian_conflict_clearance (prim.closest_approach_distance); and for every road user u other than ego that is traffic (ru.aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-285::traffic) and occupies I, the same with p.conflict_clearance. With no such road user in the scene the duty is met.

narrowings.why: The danger of a crash the right-of-way presupposes is read as a projected close approach of the centres under constant velocities; 'lawfully' is not read, so the yield is owed to every pedestrian within an adjacent crosswalk and every member of traffic within the intersection (the lawfulness of their presence refers to rules not in the library).

segmentation.text: A signal of intention to turn right or left, or otherwise turn a vehicle from a direct course, shall be given continuously during
not less than the last 100 feet traveled
in a business or residential district
and not less than the last 300 feet traveled
in any other area
prior to changing the course of a vehicle.
This rule shall be observed, regardless of the weather.

elements.justification: A signal 'of intention' is the signal itself: sig.turn_indicator, 'the turn indicator state ∈ {off, left, right}', or sig.hand_signal, 'a driver's or rider's arm signal; meaning ∈ {no_signal, left, right, stop_or_slow, re_enter}', on the side of the turn ('to turn right or left, or otherwise turn ... from a direct course'), the turn itself being read by t8's concepts. 'given continuously during' is that matching signal at every observation of the window (holdsFor): an observation with the indicator off and no matching arm signal breaks it. 'Not a stand-in for: the turn or lane change itself' is respected: the signal is judged separately from the turn. 'a vehicle' is DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle ('every device in, upon or by which any person or property is or may be transported or drawn upon a highway', except 'Devices moved by human power', 'Electric bicycles', electric personal assistive mobility devices and 'An electric scooter'), claimed whole.

'the last 100 feet traveled' is a window measured in the distance ego travelled behind the onset (a .path window), read through kin.path_length, 'distance travelled along the body's path since the start of the trace, monotone'; the figure is the law's literal. It selects the window where t5 holds.
'the last 300 feet traveled' is the same .path window with the law's other literal, through kin.path_length; it selects the window where t7 holds.

'changing the course of a vehicle' is a change of its heading to one side from an observed onset: drv.motion.left_turn_from_onset or drv.motion.right_turn_from_onset, each recognizing a continuous turning stretch whose heading change reaches the turn angle. 'prior to' places the window before the observed onset: the observation at which drv.motion.turning_left (or drv.motion.turning_right) last became true before the recognition, as those concepts' act records declare it. 'a vehicle' is DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle, claimed whole.

assumptions.meaning: The map or the trace declares the territory at the road user's position a business district or a residence district.
The map or the trace declares the territory at the road user's position a business district or a residence district.

residues.why: The duty holds in every weather: no condition of the weather restricts it, so the duty is the same whether or not its words hold.

applicability: ego is a vehicle (ru.aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle). The judged observation is the recognition of a left turn from an observed onset (drv.motion.left_turn_from_onset with p.left_turn_min_angle, p.turn_yaw_tolerance, p.rest_speed_tolerance, p.heading_since_step_carla_scene_graph) or of a right turn from an observed onset (drv.motion.right_turn_from_onset with p.right_turn_min_angle and the same tolerances).
obligation: Event, recognition and history (rule 4d): the event is the change of course; it is recognized at the judged observation; its observed onset is the last observation at which drv.motion.turning_left (for a left turn; drv.motion.turning_right for a right turn, each with p.turn_yaw_tolerance and p.rest_speed_tolerance) became true, the turning state having held at every observation since (a since operator: turning since (rise of turning and W)). W, read at that onset: where asm.business_or_residence_district holds there, at every observation of the window of the literal 100 ft of path travelled by ego behind the onset (holdsFor .path, kin.path_length), ego's turn indicator is left (sig.turn_indicator = left) or its arm signal means left (sig.hand_signal = left); where it does not hold, the same over the window of the literal 300 ft. For a right turn the matching side is right. The window ends at the onset and is the words' own bound; a window that reaches past the start of the recording is unknown (windowTruncated), as is the duty where the assumption is undeclared and the two windows decide differently. Conduct after the onset is not read.

narrowings.why: A change of course is read as a turn whose heading change from its observed onset reaches the turn angle; a lane change or a gentle departure from the course, whose heading change stays below it, is not read, and a road bend followed through that angle in one turning stretch is read as a turn.

segmentation.text: Upon any highway
outside of a business or residence district
no person shall stop, park or leave standing
any vehicle,
whether attended or unattended,
upon the paved or main-traveled part of the highway
when it is practicable to stop, park or so leave such vehicle off such part of the highway,
but in every event
an unobstructed width of the highway opposite a standing vehicle shall be left
for the free passage of other vehicles
and a clear view of such stopped vehicles shall be available from a distance of 200 feet in each direction upon such highway.

This section shall not apply to the driver of any vehicle which is disabled while on the paved or main-traveled portion of a highway in such manner and to such extent that it is impossible to avoid stopping and temporarily leaving such disabled vehicle in such position.

elements.justification: st.highway is 'the entire public way between its boundary lines, including sidewalks and shoulders', carrying DEF-NRS-484A-095 ('the entire width between the boundary lines of every way dedicated to a public authority'); ego's footprint overlapping it (rel.occupies). 'Not a stand-in for: the roadway' is respected: the part of it the duty reads is e6.

'stop' where prohibited is DEF-NRS-484A-260, 'any halting, even momentarily, of a vehicle, whether occupied or not, except when necessary to avoid conflict with other traffic or in compliance with the directions of a police officer or official traffic-control device'; 'park' (DEF-NRS-484A-155) and 'standing' (DEF-NRS-484A-250) are halts too, so their union is a halt (drv.motion.at_rest) other than the excepted ones, which the rule carries beside it: a halt behind a road user ahead in ego's lane (rel.ahead_behind_in_lane) that is itself at rest within p.queue_gap (rel.surface_gap), or a halt while a stop indication governs ego's carrier (dev.governs of a dev.traffic_signal displaying circular_red or a red_arrow, a dev.stop_sign, or a dev.human_direction indicating stop). 'no person shall' is read through the vehicle's halt (observable_reading agency).
'vehicle' admitted as DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle ('every device in, upon or by which any person or property is or may be transported or drawn upon a highway', with its exceptions), claimed whole.

'the paved or main-traveled part of the highway': the main-traveled part is the roadway (st.roadway, 'the part of a highway improved for vehicular traffic, excluding shoulder'), the paved part also a shoulder whose paved attribute holds (st.shoulder, 'paved attribute'); ego's footprint overlaps one (rel.occupies) lying on the highway of e1 (st.on_way).

Nearest atoms only, to show the shortfall (gap on e13): that a vehicle is disabled so that it cannot avoid stopping is a condition of the vehicle no atom carries; hazard lamps (sig.hazard, 'both indicators flashing together') are a lamp state, and an engine stopped (kin.engine_running) is 'Not a stand-in for: motion or a halt' nor for a vehicle that cannot move.

operationalizations.convention: Off-road standing place within braking reach: halting off the paved or main-traveled part is practicable where a region off it lies within p.offroad_stop_reach of the halted vehicle's body (drv.position.near_region over st.region_geometry): a shoulder whose paved attribute does not hold (st.shoulder) or a parking space (st.parking_space) that does not overlap the roadway. The distance to the nearest such place enters the bound.

assumptions.meaning: The map or the trace declares the territory at the road user's position a business district or a residence district.

residues.why: Whether the vehicle is attended or unattended does not change the duty: it is the same whether or not its words hold.

applicability: ego is a vehicle; at the judged observation ego occupies a roadway, or a shoulder whose paved attribute holds, lying on a highway (st.on_way), asm.business_or_residence_district does not hold there, and ego is halted (drv.motion.at_rest with p.rest_speed_tolerance) other than behind a road user ahead in its lane at rest within p.queue_gap or under a stop indication governing its carrier. Exception: a disabled vehicle (gap on e13).
obligation: It is not the case that a region off the paved or main-traveled part (a shoulder whose paved attribute does not hold, or a parking space not overlapping the roadway) lies within p.offroad_stop_reach of ego's body (drv.position.near_region over st.region_geometry).

narrowings.why: 'no person shall' is read through the vehicle's halt, whoever controls it.
Practicability is read only through an off-road standing place within reach; its size and surface are not read.

'a clear view of such stopped vehicles shall be available from a distance of 200 feet in each direction' is st.sight_distance at the place ego stands, at or above the law's literal: 'the distance along the road within which a vehicle at a point and another vehicle on the road could see each other ... both the view of approaching traffic from that point and its being seen by drivers approaching it'. Its exclusions (whether an actual road user saw it, rel.visible; the clarity of the air, env.visibility) do not apply: the duty is the view of the place, whether or not anyone approaches. 'in each direction' is read through that single value (narrowing).
Nearest atoms only, to show the shortfall (gap on e13): a disabled vehicle is a condition no atom carries; sig.hazard is a lamp state and kin.engine_running is 'Not a stand-in for: motion or a halt'.

obligation: The sight distance at ego's place (st.sight_distance) is at or above the literal 200 ft.

segmentation.text: It is unlawful for any person to drive or operate
a vehicle of any kind or character
at: A rate of speed
greater than is reasonable or proper, having due regard for the traffic, surface and width of the highway, the weather and other highway conditions.

elements.justification: 'to drive or operate' is read through the vehicle's controlled motion (observable_reading agency): its speed (kin.speed, 'magnitude of velocity'), whoever or whatever controls it.

'vehicle' admitted as DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle: 'every device in, upon or by which any person or property is or may be transported or drawn upon a highway', except 'Devices moved by human power or used exclusively upon stationary rails', 'Electric bicycles', electric personal assistive mobility devices and 'An electric scooter'; claimed whole. 'of any kind or character' adds no restriction.
'A rate of speed' is kin.speed, 'magnitude of velocity' in m/s; kin.accel_longitudinal's 'Not a stand-in for: speed' confirms speed is read directly.

operationalizations.standard: a rate of speed greater than is reasonable or proper, having due regard for the traffic, surface and width of the highway, the weather and other highway conditions
operationalizations.convention: Stopping-sight-distance model of highway design (AASHTO Green Book), with the curve side-friction and lane-width relations of the same guides. Surface and weather select the deceleration: p.stopping_decel_ice where env.ice_or_snow holds, else p.stopping_decel_wet where env.wet_road or env.precipitation holds, else p.stopping_decel_dry (Term.cond over drv.motion.stopping_distance calls with p.perception_reaction_time). The stopping distance may not exceed the sight distance of the place (st.sight_distance) nor the visibility distance (env.visibility); for every road user ahead of ego in its lane (rel.ahead_behind_in_lane), the traffic, the gap (rel.surface_gap) may not fall below the speed times p.perception_reaction_time; the speed squared times the curvature (st.curvature) may not exceed p.curve_lateral_accel; the speed times p.lane_width_speed_time may not exceed the width (st.lane_width) of the lane ego occupies (st.lane, rel.occupies). Each measured magnitude enters its bound. The standard is the whole duty: the rule is a surrogate.

applicability: ego is a vehicle (ru.aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle); the duty is judged at every observation.
obligation: At every observation, with D the stopping distance of ego (drv.motion.stopping_distance with p.perception_reaction_time and the deceleration selected by Term.cond: p.stopping_decel_ice where env.ice_or_snow holds, else p.stopping_decel_wet where env.wet_road or env.precipitation holds, else p.stopping_decel_dry): D is at or below st.sight_distance at ego's place and at or below env.visibility; ego's speed (kin.speed) squared times st.curvature at its place is at or below p.curve_lateral_accel; for every lane l ego occupies (rel.occupies), ego's speed times p.lane_width_speed_time is at or below st.lane_width of l; and for every road user u other than ego that is ahead of ego in its lane (rel.ahead_behind_in_lane), the gap between them (rel.surface_gap) is at or above ego's speed times p.perception_reaction_time. With no such road user the last clause is met.

narrowings.why: 'drive or operate' is read through the vehicle's motion, whoever or whatever controls it.

The factors are read only through the contracts named: traffic through the road users ahead in ego's lane (crossing and oncoming traffic, and its density, are not read); surface through wet and icy or snow-covered states; width through the width of the lane ego occupies; weather through precipitation and visibility distance; the catch-all 'other highway conditions' only through curvature and the sight distance of the place (grade, darkness and works are not read).

param_proposals.name: p.perception_reaction_time
param_proposals.convention: Brake reaction time of the stopping-sight-distance model: the time from the appearance of a hazard to the application of the brakes.
param_proposals.source: AASHTO Green Book, stopping sight distance

param_proposals.name: p.stopping_decel_dry
param_proposals.convention: Deceleration a driver attains in a controlled stop on a dry paved surface.
param_proposals.source: AASHTO Green Book and braking studies (Fambro et al., NCHRP 400)

param_proposals.name: p.stopping_decel_wet
param_proposals.convention: Deceleration of the stopping-sight-distance model, which most drivers attain on a wet pavement.
param_proposals.source: AASHTO Green Book, stopping sight distance

param_proposals.name: p.stopping_decel_ice
param_proposals.convention: Deceleration attainable on an icy or snow-covered surface, from the low friction coefficient of such surfaces.
param_proposals.source: winter road friction measurements (PIARC)

param_proposals.name: p.curve_lateral_accel
param_proposals.convention: Side-friction limit of horizontal curve design: the lateral acceleration a curve may impose on a vehicle at a comfortable, safe speed.
param_proposals.source: AASHTO Green Book, horizontal curve side friction factors

param_proposals.name: p.lane_width_speed_time
param_proposals.convention: Lane width per unit of speed from the lane-width and design-speed relation of highway design guides (a full-width lane for a high design speed): the speed times it may not exceed the lane's width.
param_proposals.source: AASHTO Green Book lane widths by design speed

contract: The heading change of road user a since it entered region r: the signed change of the direction its body points (degrees, left positive), accumulated from the observation at which a's footprint last came to overlap r, where it is zero, to the observation, whether or not a still overlaps r. Measured by integrating a's yaw rate (kin.yaw_rate, deg/s, left positive) from the observation at which a's occupancy of r (rel.occupies) last became true, with the step bound, the largest interval between consecutive observations integrated across. It is unknown where that entry is not observed (a occupied r from the start of the recording, or an unknown occupancy could hide the entry), where an interval between consecutive observations since the observation before the entry exceeds the step bound, or where a yaw rate since the entry is missing. Not a stand-in for a turn: it is a magnitude that a caller bounds, and a road user that follows a bend of the way through r accumulates the bend's heading change.

params.name: step
params.meaning: the step bound: the largest interval between consecutive observations the integration crosses

elements.span: the observation at which a's occupancy of r (rel.occupies) last became true
elements.justification: rel.occupies is 'a road user's footprint overlaps a lane / region'; its rise marks the entry from which the heading change is counted.

elements.span: integrating a's yaw rate (kin.yaw_rate, deg/s, left positive)
elements.justification: kin.yaw_rate is the 'rate of change of heading, positive when the heading turns to the left'; its exclusion 'Not a stand-in for: road curvature' is stated in the contract: the concept counts the road user's own heading change, bend or turn alike.

scenarios.name: fails
scenarios.narrative: a crosses r without turning; the value read at the exit stays near zero, outside the instance's left band.

scenarios.name: blind
scenarios.narrative: as in holds, but the source supplies no yaw rate, so the heading change is unknown.

contract: Road user a is turning to the right at an observation: it moves and its heading turns to the right. Measured as a not at rest (drv.motion.at_rest with the speed tolerance does not hold) and its yaw rate (kin.yaw_rate, deg/s, left positive) at or below the negative of the yaw tolerance, the rate below which a change of heading counts as none. A state at each observation while a turn is under way, not a completed manoeuvre: it does not say how far the turn goes, and it holds alike where the road user follows a bend of the road to the right. Not a stand-in for the turn indicator or for a declared intention to turn.

params.meaning: the yaw rate magnitude below which a change of heading counts as none

params.name: speed_tolerance
params.meaning: the speed at or below which the road user counts as at rest

elements.span: a not at rest (drv.motion.at_rest with the speed tolerance does not hold)
elements.justification: drv.motion.at_rest holds at each observation at which the speed is at or below the speed tolerance; its negation is the road user moving.

elements.span: its yaw rate (kin.yaw_rate, deg/s, left positive) at or below the negative of the yaw tolerance
elements.justification: kin.yaw_rate is 'positive when the heading turns to the left', so a rightward turn is a yaw rate below the negative tolerance; 'Not a stand-in for: road curvature' is stated: a bend followed to the right is included.

scenarios.name: blind

differs_from.why: the opposite hand: the yaw rate at or below the negative of the tolerance rather than at or above it

contract: Road user a turns to the left from an observed onset: over one continuous stretch in which it moves and its heading turns to the left, its heading changes to the left by at least the turn angle, the heading change below which turning counts as no change of course. Measured as drv.motion.turning_left (with the yaw tolerance and the speed tolerance) holding at every observation since the observation at which it last became true, and the heading change since that observation (integrated from kin.yaw_rate, degrees, left positive, with the step bound, the largest interval between consecutive observations integrated across) at or above the turn angle. The act's observed beginning is the observation at which drv.motion.turning_left last became true. The act is recognized at the observation at which the heading change since that beginning first reaches the turn angle. The concept holds at the recognition observation only. Conduct before the observed beginning is no part of the act, and where that beginning is not observed (the stretch began before the recording, or an unknown turning state could hide its start) whether the act occurred is unknown. A stretch that ends before its heading change reaches the turn angle is no turn; a road user that follows a bend of the way through that angle turns in this sense. Not a stand-in for the turn indicator or a declared intention to turn, nor for a lane change, whose heading change stays below the turn angle.

contract: The distance road user a would travel before coming to rest if it began to brake after a reaction time, at the observation: its speed (kin.speed, m/s) times the reaction time, plus the square of its speed divided by twice the deceleration (m). Computed from the current speed only, under a constant deceleration on a level road. Not a stand-in for a sight distance or a gap to another road user, which a caller compares it with, nor for a braking manoeuvre actually made.

params.meaning: the time from the appearance of a hazard to the application of the brakes

params.meaning: the constant deceleration of the braking

elements.justification: kin.speed is the 'magnitude of velocity' in m/s; the distance is computed from it alone, with the caller's reaction time and deceleration.

literals.why: the factor of the braking distance: the square of the speed divided by twice the deceleration
